name: cross_model_attention_kv_ablation_2wiki_seed1234
alignment: Unicode character offsets projected onto identical whitespace-delimited text units, including following whitespace; boundary tokens receive fractional mass
protocol: Native chat per model, identical evidence/question/forced answer prefix, Qwen thinking=False; no answer content in prefix. Oracle supporting sentences plus fixed distractors are a controlled evidence subset, not the official full-context benchmark.
ablation: Mask selected evidence KV key columns for every attention head/layer during forced-prefix and answer continuation only. Keep positions, cached body and token order fixed. This measures direct cached-KV access, not removal of indirectly propagated information.
caveats: No model or matching parameters are trained. Head assignment uses only eight calibration questions; sixteen disjoint questions are used for reported evaluation.
Rectangular one-to-one head assignment leaves extra heads unmatched; report coverage. Matching is not evidence of semantic equivalence.
Gemma FP32 versus Llama/Qwen FP16 is a recorded hardware adaptation, not precision-matched architecture isolation.
Short-answer conditional NLL and greedy EM are diagnostic metrics on a small evidence-conditioned pilot.
